newsitem.title: SPAIN: Clintons in Majorca for pre-summit interlude.
newsitem.headline: Clintons in Majorca for pre-summit interlude.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary arrived in this Mediterranean island resort on Saturday for a weekend holiday before the July 8-9 NATO summit in Madrid.

The Clintons, who flew in from Washington aboard Air Force One, were to be guests of Spain's King Juan Carlos and Queen Sophia at Alamundaina Palace, a 10th century Moorish castle overlooking Palma's yacht-filled harbour.
Their interlude in Majorca, one of southern Europe's busiest tourist spots, started an eight-day trip that was also to take the U.S. president to Poland, Romania and Denmark.
In Madrid, Clinton and leaders of NATO's 15 other member states were to begin expanding the alliance into former communist central and eastern Europe.
Despite a French-led clamour to also add Romania and Slovenia, the first round of enlargement was expected to be limited to three countries: Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.

Another highlight of the two-day NATO summit was to be the signing of a charter of friendship and cooperation between the alliance and Ukraine. The document is modelled on an agreement between NATO and Russia signed in Paris in May which aims to create a new pan-European security order in the aftermath of the Cold War.
